s1.syndrome_frame: a 27-year-old man with a history of melanoma presents with respiratory symptoms and multiple masses
salient_findings: a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe
an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone
key_facts: 27-year-old man
history of 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck
treated six years earlier by wide local excision
no sentinel lymph node biopsy
no adjuvant therapy
presents with hemoptysis and dyspnea
vital signs were within normal limits
physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor
laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, were unremarkable
contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed a mass in the right lower lobe
endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation
PET/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass and an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone

shortlist.why_kept: history of melanoma and presence of multiple masses

shortlist.why_kept: hyoid lesion suspected to be a synchronous primary bone tumor

raw.rationale: Molecular studies were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) despite being negative for an EWSR1 translocation, and the patient's response to chemotherapy typical for Ewing sarcoma supports this diagnosis for the lung lesion

rejected.label: Melanoma metastasis
rejected.why: The lung lesion's molecular characteristics and response to chemotherapy are not typical for melanoma metastasis

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: The presentation and molecular findings do not align with plasmacytoma, which typically involves plasma cell neoplasms

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: The description of the lung lesion as a malignant small round blue cell tumor does not match the typical histology of chondrosarcoma

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: While molecular studies suggested consistency with PNET, Ewing sarcoma is a more specific diagnosis within the PNET category and better explains the clinical presentation
